text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Expectations growing that French government may go ahead with partial privatisation of France Telecom
-- Government forced to delay release of Social Security accounts. Provisional deficit nears 36 billion francs in 1997
-- Paris Bourse surges higher, breaks records
-- Daimler Benz unit Debis decides to put 24.4 percent stake in French computer services company Cap Gemini up for sale

-- Boeing ready to make concessions to European Commission. Aircraft-maker could give up its exclusive contracts in exchange for green light from Commission in Brussels for merger with McDonnel Douglas
--Jean-Pierre Gerard, member of the Bank of France monetary policy council, says the lowering of short term rates in Europe remains linked to progress on budgets
-- Government family allowance reforms will bring in four to six billion francs to public coffers
-- Head of Communist-led CGT Louis Viannet says any austerity drive by Socialist-led government in the autumn would provoke a "a very strong clash"
-- French cabinet approves four percent rise in national minimum wage
